clue.text: Second merchant doesn't finish wine

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second

indicators.note: not finishing means the merchant word loses its final letter

parts.note: a merchant is a seller

explanation.surface: A wine dealer leaves the job half done.
explanation.definitionFit: Moselle is a white wine from the valley of the river Moselle in Germany.

clue.text: It darkens fringes of a woman's outlook on things

definitions.text: It darkens fringes of a woman's outlook on things

parts.words: It darkens fringes of a woman's outlook on things
parts.note: the fringes are eyelashes around the eyes through which she looks out on the world

explanation.surface: Something gloomy colouring a woman's view of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlook' suggests attitude, but here it means the eyes, and the fringes are the lashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic applied to eyelashes makes them darker and thicker.

clue.text: Racing around oarsman in small republic

indicators.note: racing about suggests the letters are rushing around into a new order

explanation.surface: A rowing race takes place in a tiny state.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny republic surrounded by Italy.

clue.text: Machine makes one nearly sweat

indicators.note: nearly means the sweat word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: lather is the frothy sweat of a horse, or a state of agitation

explanation.surface: Working a machine makes one break out in a sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes one' is a link: LATHER, a sweat, loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine tool that spins a workpiece against a cutting tool.

clue.text: Made ready?

parts.note: ready is slang for cash, so making ready means making money

explanation.surface: Asking if something has been prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' looks like 'prepared', but 'the ready' is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Money made by work is money gained as wages.

clue.text: Follow and prosper

explanation.surface: Advice to imitate someone and do well.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow is to come after someone in office or in time, and to prosper is to achieve success.

clue.text: It's more detestable when hooter's used

definitions.text: It's more detestable when hooter's used

parts.words: It's more detestable when hooter's used
parts.note: the hooter is the nose: something worse to sniff is more offensive

explanation.surface: Something is more annoying when a car horn is sounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a car horn, but it is slang for the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more offensive to the nose has a stronger bad odour.

clue.text: Look around inside cooked chapati for a sausage

indicators.note: inside means it is placed within the other letters
cooked suggests the letters are reworked into a new arrangement
turning around means the look word is read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word for look

explanation.surface: Peering into the flatbread to find a banger.
explanation.walkthrough: OL (LO turned 'around') goes 'inside' CHIPATA, the anagram of CHAPATI signalled by 'cooked'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin pork sausage, often served at Christmas.

clue.text: Chemical damaged trees

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A chemical that has harmed the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is a compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Piece of furniture helps actor get ready

explanation.surface: Someone in the theatre wings with a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: A theatre dresser helps actors into their costumes.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen cupboard with shelves, and a backstage assistant who helps with costumes.

clue.text: Politician takes Japanese money to register returns

parts.note: the sen is a small Japanese coin

indicators.note: returning means the register word is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a list or register of duties

explanation.surface: A politician pocketing yen before filing a tax return.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an elected lawmaker.

clue.text: I sleep, taking time to rewrite long letter

indicators.note: rewriting the letters puts them into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer dozes off before revising a lengthy letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of I, SLEEP and T (for time) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal or lengthy letter, like those of the apostles in the Bible.

clue.text: What Venus de Milo might have said? How novel!

definitions.text: What Venus de Milo might have said? How novel!

parts.words: What Venus de Milo might have said? How novel!
parts.note: the famous armless statue bidding goodbye to her arms, which is also the title of a Hemingway novel

explanation.surface: Imagining the words of the armless statue in the Louvre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venus de Milo has lost her arms; 'How novel!' points to Hemingway's 1929 novel of that title.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's war novel title reads literally as a goodbye to one's limbs.

clue.text: Thin plate around creature

indicators.note: turning around means the thin plate word is read backwards

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: A thin sheet of metal wrapped round a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Any creature, such as a dog or bird, is an animal.

clue.text: Birdie? Better than that!

parts.note: in golf a birdie is one under par; a large seabird also names a score three under par

explanation.surface: Praise for a golfer's very good hole.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf a birdie is one under par and an eagle two under; the large seabird's name is the score three under par.
explanation.definitionFit: A big seabird gives its name to a golf score of three strokes under par.

clue.text: 12 is unable to fit in bottle

indicators.note: fitting in means one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: refers to the answer to 12 across, a creature: a deer is one
can't means is unable

explanation.surface: An animal that cannot squeeze into a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' stands for its answer, a creature, here a DEER; CANT (can't) goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass bottle into which wine or spirits are poured for serving.

clue.text: It's just like a T-Rex to be appetising

explanation.surface: A dinosaur finds something tasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The word read literally means having lots of teeth, as the dinosaur did.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally it means full of fangs, and its everyday sense is tasty or delicious.

clue.text: Asian relation touring

indicators.note: touring suggests the letters travel round into a new order

explanation.surface: A relative travelling in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental is an old word for things from East Asia.

clue.text: We hear they're prized as openers!

definitions.text: We hear they're prized as openers!

parts.words: We hear they're prized as openers!
parts.note: levers used to force things open are prised in; prized sounds the same, and they open things

explanation.surface: Something valued as a good way to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prized' is a sound-alike for 'prised': these iron bars prise lids and doors open.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron levers with a bent end are used to force open boxes or doors.

clue.text: Primrose threatens with impudent talk

parts.note: cows means intimidates or threatens
lip is cheek, impudent talk

explanation.surface: A flower that bullies with cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a wild flower of the primula family, a kind of primrose.

clue.text: A party on opening Western temple? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading from right to left
quite the opposite tells us the order just built is to be flipped round

parts.note: a do is a party
a gap is an opening

explanation.surface: Throwing a party at the opening of a temple in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: A, DO and GAP are written in a row; 'Western' (right to left in an across clue) and 'Quite the opposite' both turn the run round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a temple in East Asia.

clue.text: Checks collars

explanation.surface: Inspections of shirt necks.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop or halt something, and to seize or nab a suspect, as police do.

clue.text: One's going to court around Circle Line

indicators.note: around means the other letters sit either side of the circle

parts.note: one is I, and the 's is is
the bar is the court, where barristers practise
O is round like a circle

explanation.surface: Someone heads to court on the Circle Line of the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: IS and BAR sit 'around' O. The Circle Line is a London Underground line.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining points of equal pressure.

clue.text: Painting of birds by a lepidopterist?

parts.note: whistlers are a family of Australasian songbirds
someone who hunts moths could be called a moth-er

explanation.surface: A gallery picture of birds painted by a butterfly collector.
explanation.walkthrough: A moth collector is styled a 'moth-er'; the painting is James McNeill Whistler's portrait of his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistler's 1871 portrait of his mother is one of the most famous American paintings.

clue.text: Champion missing wide part of target

indicators.note: missing means the wide letter is taken away

parts.note: a winner is a champion
W is the cricket abbreviation for wide

explanation.surface: A champion archer misses the target.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner is the ring of an archery or shooting target just outside the bull.

clue.text: Work on spasmodic moment of vision

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a tic is a sudden spasm

explanation.surface: An operation done in a flash of insight.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic means relating to the eye or sight.

clue.text: Ruffian's entertaining in European Rugby move

indicators.note: entertaining means holding the other letters inside

parts.note: a lout is a ruffian; the 's stands for is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hooligan hosts a sports move somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A line-out is the restart in rugby union when the ball is thrown in between two lines of players.

clue.text: They secure pantomime page boy

explanation.surface: Fasteners and a character from a Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pantomime, the Christmas family stage show, Buttons is Cinderella's friend, the page boy at the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Small discs fasten clothes, and Buttons is the page in the pantomime Cinderella.

clue.text: Soldiers look around in the shade

parts.note: paras are paratroopers, soldiers

indicators.note: turning around means the look word is read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word for look

explanation.surface: Troops peering about from the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella giving shade from the sun.

clue.text: Insects don't start disease

indicators.note: not starting means the insect word loses its first letter

parts.note: crickets are chirping insects

explanation.surface: Bugs that never begin spreading illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rickets is a bone-softening illness caused by lack of vitamin D.
